title: reactor-api splits HTTP transport from GraphQL execution behind IHttpAdapter and IGatewayAdapter, with a Fetch-API FetchHandler as the only contract between them
content:
`reactor-api` separates GraphQL and HTTP concerns into two independent interfaces so the HTTP framework (currently Express) or the GraphQL engine (currently Apollo) can be replaced without touching application logic.

**`IHttpAdapter`** owns the transport: binding ports, registering routes, and bridging framework-native request/response objects into Fetch API types. `setupMiddleware(config)` installs CORS and body parsing once; `mount(path, handler, opts?)` registers a handler with `exact: false` (default, exact-path match in an internal dispatch map) or `exact: true` (prefix match, router `.use()` semantics); `getRoute` registers read-only GET routes such as `/health` and `/explorer`; `mountRawMiddleware` takes a Connect/Express-compatible function (the Vite dev server) with the cast to the native type **contained inside the adapter**, so call sites need no framework imports; `listen(port, tls?)` returns the `http.Server` so callers can attach WebSocket servers and supports three TLS modes — `true` (devcert), `{ keyPath, certPath }`, or in-memory `{ cert, key }`. `handle` is a read-only escape hatch to the raw framework object, documented for integrations with no framework-agnostic equivalent yet.

**`IGatewayAdapter<TContext>`** owns GraphQL: `createHandler(schema, contextFactory)` for one subgraph, `createSupergraphHandler(...)` composing all subgraphs via federation, `updateSupergraph()` re-composing the SDL and hot-reloading the running gateway (a no-op before the supergraph handler exists), `attachWebSocket(...)` returning a `WsDisposer`, and `start` / `stop`.

The contract between them is one type:

```ts
type FetchHandler = (request: Request) => Promise<Response>;
```

"No Express types cross this boundary." That is the whole point — the gateway produces `FetchHandler`s and the HTTP adapter consumes them.
